en.title: Hark! The Herald Angels Sing
en.author: Charles Wesley
stanzas:
[G]Hark! The her[D]ald an[G]gels sing,
[D]Glory to [C]the [Am]newborn [G]King;
Peace on earth, [D]and [Em]mercy mild,
[A7]God and sinners re[G]con[D]ciled!
[G]Joyful, all ye [C]nations [D]rise,
[G]Join the triumph [C]of the [D]skies;
[C]With th'angel[E7]ic [Am]host proclaim,
[D7]Christ is [G]born in Beth[D7]le[G]hem!

Hail the heav'nly Prince of Peace!
Hail the Sun of Righteousness!
Light and life to all He brings,
Ris'n with healing in His wings.
Mild He lays His glory by,
Born that man no more may die.
Born to raise the sons of earth,
Born to give them second birth.

Come, desire of nations, come,
Fix in us Thy humble home;
Rise, the woman's conquering Seed,
Bruise in us the serpent's head.
Now display Thy saving power,
Ruined nature now restore;
Now in mystic union join
Thine to ours, and ours to Thine.

Adam's likeness, Lord, efface,
Stamp Thine image in its place:
Second Adam from above,
Reinstate us in Thy love.
Let us Thee, though lost, regain,
Thee, the Life, the inner man:
O, to all Thyself impart,
Formed in each believing heart.

notes: Text: Cyber Hymnal's standard (Whitefield-altered, 1753) version in five stanzas; most hymnals print only the first three, and hymnary's representative text is those three. Wesley's 1739 original ('Hark, how all the welkin rings') is a different text and is not used here. Tune MENDELSSOHN (Felix Mendelssohn 1840, adapted by W. H. Cummings 1856); hymnary lists F and G as the common printed keys, so G is used and the chart is the Cyber Hymnal MIDI (mid/m/e/n/d/mendelssohn.mid) transposed F->G. All eight stanza lines and both refrain lines align seven-syllables-to-seven-onsets with the melody, so placements are note-accurate; the E7-Am turn in line 7 is the tune's own secondary dominant, not an embellishment. Chart corrected 2026-08-02: the MIDI-derived chart ended stanza line 8 and the refrain on D7 (V7) and put I under 'nations rise'/'of the skies' where the harmony is IV-V; fixed against two independent published charts that agree (traditionalsongs.org/hark-the-herald-angels-sing.html and hymnal.net/en/hymn/h/84), so both final cadences now land on G. Text cross-checked 2026-08-02 against Timeless Truths, which prints a four-stanza version (st. 4 merges the Cyber Hymnal's st. 4-5) with identical wording in st. 2-3.
